what: Which zone name a series repeats on: every stored name and the answer cal_core::series_clock_zone gives, and every tzdata name and the zone cal_core::canonical_zone resolves it to.
why: The views, the reminders and the stamp on a new series each decided on their own which names are a zone. The views took every name but `UTC`; the reminders trimmed the name and knew it only in its exact case; a series Exchange stored as `Etc/UTC` took the zoned path in the views. One rule in the core answers all three, and a frontend that is not JavaScript.
decidedBy: DESIGN-series-time-zone.md, section "UTC und Anbieter", and the decisions of 2026-09-14: a name counts only if tzdata knows it (ASCII case ignored, nothing trimmed) and it is not one of the eighteen names tzdata gives UTC. Everything else repeats on UTC, in the views and in the reminders alike. The answers are chosen, not measured: the rule replaces three different ones.
writtenBy: By hand, from the tzdata chrono-tz 0.10.4 ships (release 2025b): the files `backward` and `etcetera` for the links, the zone files for the zones.
readBy: crates/cal-ffi/src/lib.rs (the door tests: every row through the phone's door)
src/intl/seriesClock.contract.test.ts (every row through the WebAssembly door and the shared shell)

whereItLives.note: Inside cal-core, like normalizeJoinUrl.json: twelve adapter repositories compile cal-core, and an include_str! reaching out of the crate would break the day it moves. A crate reads its own files.

notInThisTable: Whether a device's clock library can USE a zone the rule accepts (an old Android rejecting a newer name): that check stays in the shell, after the rule. Which instants a series gets on a clock: shared/contracts/eventOccurrences.json. Which zone a new series is stamped with, and how a copy keeps its zone: later stages of the design.

shape.seriesClockZone: [{tzid, zone, note}]: tzid as stored (null for none); zone is the stored spelling unchanged when the series repeats on it, null when it repeats on UTC
shape.canonicalZone: [{name, canonical, note}]: canonical is tzdata's spelling of the zone the name resolves to, null when tzdata does not know the name
shape.doors: the WebAssembly and phone doors write null as the empty string, in both directions; an empty name already means UTC, and no zone is named ''

seriesClockZone.note: No zone: the series repeats on UTC.
An empty zone is no zone.
The only UTC name the views knew before.
What Exchange stores for its own UTC and Google receives for a series without a zone. The views took the zoned path for it.
Zero offset, no daylight saving: UTC under another name.
A link to Etc/GMT, and the name a CalDAV server may write.
Nothing is trimmed: tzdata does not know the name with the space, so the series repeats on UTC, which is what it does either way.
Nothing is trimmed, so this is not Berlin. The views already repeated it on UTC, because Intl rejects the spaces; the reminders trimmed it and used Berlin. Both use UTC now.
A dotless ı (U+0131) is not an i: only ASCII letters fold. Unicode case mapping would read this as Etc/Universal.
A Windows zone name is not a tzdata name.
What V8 reports for a device set to GMT. An offset is not a tzdata name.
Intl accepts an offset as a zone, and would repeat the series on +05:30, a weekday apart near midnight, while the reminders read UTC. Not a tzdata name, so UTC for both.
What V8 reports when it cannot read the device's zone.
tzdata's placeholder zone is not in the files chrono-tz ships.
The UTC designator of a date-time is not a zone name.
An abbreviation, and an ambiguous one.
tzdata's fixed offsets run from Etc/GMT-14 to Etc/GMT+12.
Any ASCII case, and the stored spelling comes back unchanged. The views already used Berlin; the reminders, which knew names only in their exact case, used UTC. Both use Berlin now.
A link to Asia/Kolkata, and the name V8 reports for a device in India. The stored spelling comes back unchanged: an older engine may know only this one.
A link to Europe/Kyiv, and the name V8 reports for a device in Ukraine.
A link to Europe/Berlin since tzdata merged zones whose clocks agree since 1970. Still a zone, in its own spelling.
A fixed offset of eight hours west is a zone, not UTC.
An old name, still a link to America/New_York.
A link to Europe/Brussels since tzdata 2024b.
New in tzdata 2025b: a device with older zone data cannot use it, which is the shell's check, not this rule.
